newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares fall sharply in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares fall sharply in busy trade.

text.p: Shares fell sharply in trading on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday and the bourse index recorded its steepest fall for several years, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8172.05, down from 8308.12 on Monday.
The fall of over 1.6 percent was the biggest drop in one day for several years, dealers said. The maximum amount any single share is permitted to lose in one day is five percent.
Traders said the market's bearish tendencies showed no sign of easing but added that the situation could change if the government releases 1997 funds for capital expenditure soon.
"The downward trend is because of the unconducive economic environment," one dealer said.
But others blamed Tuesday's falls on moves by authorised dealers to curb the practice of the market's unregistered jobbers who are massively discounting shares in the current bear run.
The stock exchange said it would register the jobbers to regulate their activities.
Conglomerate Lever Brothers fell the maximum five percent to 24.51 naira, down 1.29 naira. PZ Industries slipped over 4.5 percent, down 1.20 naira at 24.60 naira.
Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company fell 1.30 naira to 50.00 naira and Cadbury closed 1.05 naira down at 33.75 naira.
Gainers were limited to the few shares showing recent profit increases.
AIICO Insurance rose 20 kobo to 15.00 naira while Okomu Oil Palm added four kobo to 12.84 naira.
Brewer Guinness added five kobo to 8.40 naira and newly-listed Co-operative Bank finished two kobo up at 1.11 naira.
